title: Why your electricity bill keeps growing #Eskom
text:
If Nomsa (an illustration) spent R1,000 a month on electricity, the same electricity now costs about R1,090: about R90 more a month, almost R1,100 a year. Electricity that cost R100 in 2007 costs about R1,000 now; other things that cost R100 then cost about R250. On a R12,000 salary, R1,000 is just over 8% of her pay. If electricity rises 9% a year and her pay 5% a year, in five years it takes about 10%.

About the example: R1,000 x 1.09; R1,000 / R12,000 = 8.3%; after five years 1,538.62 / 15,315.38 = 10.05%.

Full guide: "How Eskom Went Broke, and What It Costs You Every Month (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.

Sources
- NERSA decisions, via EWN (10 Feb 2026) and Enerdata (16 Mar 2026): Eskom direct +8.76% (April 2026), municipalities +9.01% (July 2026)
